name: Mah Jong (Traditional Chinese)
description: Mah Jong (éº»å°‡) is a game of skill, strategy, and calculation, and it involves a degree of chance. While traditionally played with tiles, it is also frequently played with specialized 'Mahjong Cards'. Originating in China, it is played by four players. The game is similar to Rummy in that the goal is to build combinations (Sets and Runs) from a hand of 13 cards/tiles to achieve a 'Mahjong' with a 14th card.

history.origins: Developed in the mid-19th century in the Yangtze River delta, likely from earlier card games like Madiao and Khanhoo.
timeline: 1920: Abercrombie & Fitch brings Mah Jong to the USA, starting a global craze.
1949: Forbidden in mainland China during the Cultural Revolution.
1985: Re-introduced and legalized in China; remains a cultural cornerstone in Hong Kong and Taiwan.
history.cultural: Used as a social lubricant and a test of character in Chinese business and family life.
history.evolution: The game branched into dozens of regional variants (Hong Kong, Japanese Riichi, American, Taiwanese), each with different scoring and special hands.

setup.players: 4 players. Each represents a Wind (East, South, West, North).
setup.deck: 3 Suits (Circles, Bamboo, Characters) numbered 1-9 (4 of each). Winds (4 of each). Dragons (Red, Green, White - 4 of each). Plus 8 Flowers/Seasons.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards. East (dealer) starts with 14.

rules.objective: Form a valid 14-card hand consisting of four sets of three and one pair.
rules.gameplay:
1. Draw a card from the deck or 'steal' the previous discard.
2. Stealing: You can call 'Chow' (only from the player to your left), 'Pung' or 'Kong' (from anyone).
3. If you complete your 14th card, you call 'Mah Jong'.
keyRules: Each player has 13 tiles; East (dealer) has 14 to start. Win by completing 14 tiles in four melds and one pair.
Draw one tile from the wall or claim a discard to meld (Chow from left neighbor only; Pung or Kong from any). Then discard one tile.
Melds: Pung (three identical), Kong (four identical), Chow (three same suit in sequence). Declare Mah Jong when the 14th tile completes the hand.

strategy.basic: Keep your options open. Don't commit to a 'Pung' early if it ruins a potential 'Chow' sequence. A hand made mostly of Chows is easier to complete but scores fewer points.
strategy.intermediate: Efficiency (Shanten): Calculate how many cards you are away from a complete hand. If you are 'Yi-Shanten' (1 card away), focus entirely on speed rather than high points.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Discarding: If an opponent has revealed three Pungs of the same suit, never discard a card of that suit. You risk 'giving' them the winning card (Feeding the Dragon).
tips: Wait for 'Two-Sided' sequences (e.g., 4-5) rather than 'Middle' sequences (4-6).
Pay attention to 'Wall' counting. If three copies of a card are already showing, don't wait for the 4th.
